newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Vietnam offers 200,000 tns of rice to Philippines.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam offers 200,000 tns of rice to Philippines.

text.p: Vietnam has offered to sell up to 200,000 tonnes of rice to the Philippines, a senior official of the Philippine Agriculture Department said on Monday.

"Vietnam has offered to sell 100,000 tonnes of rice to the National Food Authority outright. The proposed contract also gives NFA an option to buy another 100,000 tonnes," the official who requested not to be named told Reuters.

Last week, NFA assistant administrator Vic Racho said the state-owned agency would review rice offers it got from Vietnam, Pakistan, India and China after President Fidel Ramos approved the import of up to 650,000 tonnes of rice before July 1997.
The NFA has so far bought 55,000 tonnes of Thai rice for delivery in March and April. The same agreement also gave an option to the NFA to buy an additional 150,000 tonnes.
Traders said Vietnam has offered to sell rice to the Philippines at cheaper prices, or between $5 and $10 lower than the $300 per tonne price of Thai rice it bought early this month.
The Philippine Agriculture official declined to comment on the rumoured Vietnamese price offers.
